raw_response:
I have been farming this land in Quzhou for fifty years. My body is older now but my hands still know what to do. We are just two of us at home, so I cannot take on more than I can manage. Cotton is what I know. Cotton is what this land knows. I will grow cotton on all 8 mu, same as every year.

I will buy hybrid seeds from the seed station in town. The Bt hybrid has been good to me — far fewer bollworms than the old varieties. I remember how bad the worms were before. I plant in late April, when the soil has warmed up enough. I know the feel of it.

For fertilizer, I apply compound fertilizer before plowing as a base, then top dress with urea when the plants are budding and again when bolls are setting. I do not measure with instruments — I know from the color of the leaves and how the plants look whether they are hungry. But roughly I put down what my neighbors put down and what has worked for me.

I irrigate from my well. I pump water five times — once when I transplant, once at budding, twice during flowering and boll set, and once more if it stays dry in August. My well has never failed me.

I still spray for aphids in May and again if the red spider mites come in July. And I walk the field and decide if another spray is needed. Usually four rounds is enough with the Bt cotton.

I rotary till before planting. That is what my son's tractor does for me now.

I expect around 290 jin per mu — that is what this field gives me in a normal year.
